sender.en: A new online partner, often a “foreigner”, then a fake Customs officer

name.en: Love scam: online partner, then a “parcel held at Customs” or an investment

how.en: Someone you meet on social media or a dating app builds a romance over weeks, often posing as a foreigner, and refuses or fakes video calls. They then need money for an emergency or travel, or say they sent you a gift. A fake Bureau of Customs officer calls or texts to say the parcel is held until you pay duties or fees into a personal account or e-wallet. Others steer you into crypto or forex “investments”.

text.en: A stranger starts a romance online and moves fast.
They avoid meeting, or video calls look odd.
They say they sent you a gift, or need money for an emergency.
A “Customs officer” says the parcel is held until you pay fees.
You must pay quickly, often in several payments to personal accounts.

Hello, this is Bureau of Customs NAIA. A package from the UK addressed to you, containing jewellery and USD cash, is on hold. Pay P28,500 clearance and tax to the officer’s account today or it will be confiscated.

en: online boyfriend sent a gift held at customs
customs officer asked me to pay to release a gift
met a foreigner online who asked for money
online date wants me to invest in crypto
love scam asked for money for an emergency
clearance fee for a package from my boyfriend abroad
Love that grows fast with someone you have never met.
Money for emergencies, travel or a parcel at Customs.
Payments to personal accounts or e-wallets.
Never send money to someone you have not met in person.
The Bureau of Customs never collects fees through personal accounts or e-wallets.
If you paid, call your bank or e-wallet straight away and report it to the CICC hotline 1326 or the PNP-ACG.
